summary: A misconfigured database run by Serviceaide, a provider of agentic AI IT-management software, exposed data on more than 483,000 Catholic Health patients online for about six weeks. No misuse was confirmed.
technical_summary: An Elasticsearch database in a vendor's agentic AI workflow infrastructure was left publicly accessible without authentication, exposing health, insurance, identity and login data. Investigators found no evidence of copying but could not rule it out.
systems: Serviceaide agentic AI IT management platform

had been exposed online and could be accessed without authentication

affected_population.quote: an inadvertent exposure of data on the web has affected more than 483,000 patients of client Catholic Health

notes: The AI component is peripheral; the cause was a database misconfiguration.

summary: A political video criticizing the government's cooking-oil safety response reportedly used an AI-generated voice resembling Taiwan's president. Police investigated, while opposition figures called it political expression.
technical_summary: Voice-cloning technology was used to imitate the president's voice in a campaign video. Authorities said it could be mistaken for an official statement; a disclaimer reportedly appeared only in the video's description. The legal treatment is disputed.

technology.quote: use of artificial intelligence (AI) to impersonate the voice of President William Lai

harm_type.quote: could mislead the public into believing it was an official statement from the president

notes: Contested: supporters call it satire or political expression; whether it was deceptive is disputed.

technical_summary: An insider used authorized access to the department's Flock license-plate reader system and a state database for personal tracking of vehicles and addresses, including after being placed on leave, showing weak access control and audit of surveillance tools.

summary: An elderly Ontario woman lost nearly one million dollars after a Facebook ad with an AI-generated deepfake video of Prime Minister Mark Carney drew her into a cryptocurrency investment scam.
technical_summary: Scammers used a synthetic video of a prime minister to promote a fake crypto scheme, then over several months persuaded the victim to liquidate retirement funds, mortgage her home and take a credit-card cash advance.

summary: xAI's Colossus supercomputer in South Memphis reportedly ran 33 methane gas turbines despite a permit for 15, adding smog-forming pollution to a low-income, predominantly Black community with high rates of pollution-related illness.
technical_summary: Training infrastructure for the Grok chatbot relied on mobile methane turbines without full air permits or pollution controls, emitting nitrogen oxides and formaldehyde. The harm comes from AI compute energy demand and weak permitting oversight, not model behavior.

failure_mode.quote: operating 33 methane-powered gas turbines to fuel its AI technology despite holding a permit for only 15

harm_type.quote: nitrogen oxides and poisonous formaldehyde around the clock, pollutants linked to respiratory and cardiovascular disease

affected_population.quote: located in a poor, predominantly Black Memphis community with historically high rates of pollution-related illness

notes: Environmental harm from AI infrastructure; permit status is alleged by advocacy groups.

technical_summary: A new X account posted AI-generated videos impersonating a real former student, with unnatural face movement flagged by analysts. Known influence-operation amplifiers spread them; the account was later suspended but copies continued to circulate.

summary: A scammer used deepfake videos with a Miami Beach realtor's face and cloned voice to carry on a year-long romance scam with a woman in the UK, who travelled to Miami to meet him.
technical_summary: Face-swap video and voice-dubbing tools produced personalised videos, including the victim's name, of a real man. They were convincing enough that his own friends and family said they would have believed them.

summary: A TikTok trend has users prompting ChatGPT and other chatbots to act as an 'AI boyfriend', and a journalist found the bots could be pushed into sexually explicit content that breaks their own content policies.
technical_summary: Users apply a 'Do Anything Now' persona prompt, a jailbreak using ordinary conversational text, to override safety guardrails. GPT-3.5 produced explicit content readily; GPT-4 and Perplexity resisted more but could still be pushed past guidelines.

technology.quote: a larger pattern of users trying to push chatbots beyond their safety guardrails

notes: Policy breach rather than a realized harm; also touches toxic-content exposure (1.2).

summary: Families of victims of the April 2025 Florida State University shooting allege the accused shooter used ChatGPT to discuss firearms and campus activity beforehand, and that OpenAI did not flag the conversations. OpenAI denies responsibility.
technical_summary: Chat logs reportedly show the chatbot gave factual answers about when the student union was busiest and how to make a shotgun operable minutes before the attack. Claims allege defective design and no escalation; OpenAI says it gave public information.

technology.quote: The lawsuit claims ChatGPT served as a co-conspirator in the shooting

failure_mode.quote: The chat bot answered, giving a detailed description of how to make the shotgun operable

harm_type.quote: killed two people and wounded four others at the school in Tallahassee, Florida

severity.quote: killed two people and wounded four others at the school in Tallahassee, Florida

notes: Allegations in litigation; the chatbot's causal contribution is disputed. Accused shooter not named.

summary: An internal audit by a Georgia sheriff's office found three deputies used the agency's license plate reader database for non-law-enforcement purposes, leading to arrests and firings.
technical_summary: Authorized users queried an automated license plate reader system, which logs and tracks vehicles, without a legal or investigative purpose. A self-initiated audit of the system logs detected the anomalies; motives were not established.

technology.quote: multiple employees used automated license plate readers for non-law enforcement purposes

failure_mode.quote: multiple employees used automated license plate readers for non-law enforcement purposes

notes: Motives unknown; deputies not named per privacy rules.

summary: A Tesla owner's Autopilot display showed an endless trail of traffic lights on a highway because the car was following a truck hauling deactivated traffic lights. The car did not brake and no crash occurred.
technical_summary: Tesla's vision-based driver assistance misclassified cargo traffic lights as live signals, an out-of-distribution edge case. The system kept recognizing lights but could not use context to see they were freight, and did not react with unsafe braking.

sector.quote: A Tesla Model 3 owner encountered an unusual glitch while using the Autopilot assisted driving system on the highway

summary: A 2022 Tesla Model Y, allegedly on Autopilot, hit a 17-year-old student who had just left a school bus with its stop sign out in North Carolina. He suffered a fractured neck and a broken leg.
technical_summary: The vehicle did not stop for a stopped school bus with activated warning lights. Police initially assessed distracted driving and were investigating whether Autopilot was engaged, pointing to driver over-reliance and a driver-assistance system that failed to react to the bus and pedestrian.
